title: Shastri Backs Rohit and Kohli as Ex-Cricketers Name India Squads for 2027 ODI World Cup
excerpt: Former India coach Ravi Shastri and ex-cricketers Abhinav Mukund, Manoj Tiwary, and Mohit Sharma have picked their preferred India squads for the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, igniting fierce debates over Jadeja's exclusion and the veteran presence of Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli.
body:
Shastri Goes With Experience

India's 2-1 ODI series defeat in England in July has triggered an outpouring of squad-building from cricket's pundit class, with former head coach Ravi Shastri leading the charge. Shastri, who coached India to consecutive Border-Gavaskar Trophy victories in Australia during his 2017-2021 tenure, named a 15-member squad for the 2027 World Cup that leans heavily on experience.

His picks — published via Khel Now — include Shubman Gill as captain with Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli retained in the top order. Notably, 10 of his 15 selections also featured in the 2019 World Cup squad, signalling his belief that tournament pedigree outweighs youth.

"It depends on their fitness, their hunger and, of course, form. They themselves will know by the end of this series how they feel."

— Ravi Shastri, on Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli's World Cup prospects

Shastri's pace attack comprises Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj, Mohammed Shami, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, and Arshdeep Singh — a veteran-heavy unit. He included both Ravindra Jadeja and Axar Patel as spin-bowling all-rounders, with Kuldeep Yadav as the specialist spinner.

Mukund Takes a Different Path

Former India opener Abhinav Mukund offered a contrasting vision on ESPNcricinfo's YouTube channel. His 15-member squad omitted Jadeja entirely, instead backing Axar Patel and Washington Sundar as the spin all-rounders. Mukund also left out Mohammed Shami, who has not represented India since the Champions Trophy final against New Zealand earlier this year.

Considering the pace-friendly conditions expected in southern Africa, Mukund named a five-man seam attack featuring Bumrah, Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Harshit Rana, and the emerging Gurnoor Brar — the only uncapped name across any of the selections.

Tiwary and Mohit Sharma Split on Spin

Former cricketers Manoj Tiwary and Mohit Sharma, speaking on Cricbuzz after India's 170-run victory over Afghanistan in the second ODI in June, agreed on several core picks but diverged on the crucial spin slot.

Tiwary opted for Kuldeep Yadav as his sole frontline spinner, arguing that wrist spin would be more effective on South African pitches. "You need a wrist spinner — we don't need a finger spinner on the South African pitches," Tiwary said.

Mohit Sharma, however, chose Jadeja as his only spin option, backing the veteran's batting depth and fielding brilliance. Both included Ishan Kishan as a versatile middle-order option who can keep wickets and open the batting if required, and neither found room for Axar Patel or Mohammed Siraj in their starting elevens.

The Jadeja Question

Jadeja's future in white-ball cricket has become the defining selection debate ahead of the World Cup. The 38-year-old was dropped for India's tours of Australia and England in ODIs, with selectors preferring the Axar-Washington combination.

A BCCI source told InsideSport that while Jadeja's door is not permanently shut, "it's difficult for him to make the 2027 squad. And age is also not in his favour." Jadeja himself remains hopeful, according to Cricbuzz. "Whenever I get a chance, I'll try to do what I have done all these years," he said after a Test match against the West Indies.

What's Next for India

With more than 20 ODIs remaining before the World Cup, India's management under captain Gill has time to finalise combinations. The team will host the West Indies in a limited-overs series later this year before a crucial five-match ODI series in New Zealand that will serve as the final audition for squad places.

Whether the selectors lean toward Shastri's experience-first philosophy or embrace the pace-heavy youth advocated by Mukund may well determine India's fortunes in their quest for what would be a fourth 50-over World Cup title.
